newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-SCHILLING CELEBRATES NEW DEAL AS PHILLIES EDGE PADRES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-SCHILLING CELEBRATES NEW DEAL AS PHILLIES EDGE PADRES.

text.p: Curt Schilling celebrated his new $21.95 million deal with a strong outing and Wendell Magee's solo homer broke a seventh-inning tie as the Philadelphia Phillies snapped a four-game losing streak by edging the San Diego Padres 3-2 Sunday.
Schilling, who agreed to a four-year contract extension on Thursday, limited San Diego to two runs -- one earned -- and seven hits over eight innings, walking none and striking out seven.

"It's awesome. I know I'm going to be here five years," Schilling said. "Hopefully, I'll see everything come to fruition and we'll win. I don't take that (contract) to the mound with me. You can't do that and expect to win at this level."
Schilling has given up just 20 earned runs in 19 career games against the Padres, and is 7-3 lifetime against them.
Schilling got Philadelphia's other win this year when he held Los Angeles to two infield hits over eight innings in Tuesday's season-opener.
Ricky Bottalico, who also closed the win on Opening Day, worked a perfect ninth, striking out two.
Magee was 2-for-16 this season before hitting a 2-1 pitch from Joey Hamilton (1-1) that barely cleared the centre-field fence. It was the first RBI of the season for Magee.

"Any time you're struggling at the plate and get any kind of hit, it lifts you up," Magee said. "Everything about it was just great. It won the ballgame and it picked me up going into the next series."
Quilvio Veras and Darren Daulton had solo homers for San Diego.

In Atlanta, Javy Lopez drove in a career-high four runs -- two on Saturday and two on Sunday -- as the Braves defeated the Chicago Cubs 11-5 in a game suspended by rain and resumed before Sunday's scheduled contest.

Lopez had an RBI single that tied the game in the fourth and triggered a five-run fifth inning with a run-scoring double on Saturday night. He added his first homer of the year Sunday, a two-run shot in a three-run eighth.
The game was delayed twice by rain for a total of three hours, 27 minutes on Saturday.
In the scheduled game, Greg Maddux pitched eight scoreless innings and Jeff Blauser went 3-for-3 with a homer as the Braves made quick work of the winless Cubs with a 4-0 victory.
Maddux (1-1) allowed just three hits with five strikeouts and did not walk a batter. Mark Wohlers worked the ninth in a game that took one hour, 47 minutes.
Maddux improved to 5-0 lifetime against his former team., for whom he won the first of his four straight Cy Young Awards in 1992.

In Houston, Jeff Bagwell's pinch two-run double with two out in the bottom of the eighth lifted the Astros to a 3-2 victory over the winless St. Louis Cardinals, who are off to the worst start in franchise history.

The Cardinals (0-6), an original National League club, had never lost their first six games. The defending National League Central Division champions have managed just 12 runs this year. Houston is 5-1 under new manager Larry Dierker, matching the Marlins for the best record in the N.L.

In Los Angeles, Eric Karros had a two-run single in a three-run sixth inning, Mike Piazza drove in the go-ahead run in the seventh and Todd Zeile added a two-run shot in the eighth as the Dodgers beat the Pittsburgh Pirates 6-3.
Darren Dreifort (1-0) picked up the win by allowing one hit with three strikeouts in three scoreless innings of relief. Todd Worrell pitched the ninth to record his third save in as many tries.

In Montreal, Jeff Reed had a pair of RBI singles and Kevin Ritz pitched 6 2/3 strong innings to lead the Colorado Rockies to a 6-2 victory over the Expos and their first-ever three-game sweep north of the border.
The Rockies were 6-13 lifetime at Montreal before sweeping the weekend series by a combined score of 26-9.
The win was the fourth in a row for the Rockies after two losses to give them their first winning road trip since last April 19-23 (4-1). Colorado was 28-53 on the road last season.

In Miami, Kevin Brown pitched seven strong innings and drove in a pair of runs and Jeff Conine drew a bases-loaded walk in the seventh to snap a tie as the Florida Marlins edged the Cincinnati Reds 3-2.
Brown (2-0) allowed two runs -- one earned -- six hits and three walks with five strikeouts. Felix Heredia pitched a perfect eighth and Robb Nen notched his second save.

In San Francisco, Brian Bohanon, a last-second replacement for Pete Harnisch, allowed just two runs and seven hits over seven innings as the New York Mets salvaged the finale of a three-game series with a 4-2 victory over the Giants.
Bohanon (1-0), activated off the disabled list hours earlier, walked one and struck out five. Greg McMichael and John Franco finished up.
Harnisch was a late scratch after suffering from insomnia during his attempt to end his smokeless tobacco habit.
